newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Mubarak urges Israel to honour peace accords.
newsitem.headline: Mubarak urges Israel to honour peace accords.

text.p: Egypt's President Hosni Mubarak called on Israel on Sunday to implement "faithfully" recent Middle East accords, implicitly warning that delay could undermine Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.

Mubarak was speaking at a news conference just before holding his first formal talks in six months with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Mubarak, Netanyahu and Arafat are in Davos for the World Economic Forum.

"Since the (Hebron) agreement was signed, I think Israel should faithfully implement the agreement," the Egyptian leader said, referring to last month's accord on transfer of most of the West Bank town to Palestinian control.
But he said that, in talks with Arafat in Davos on Saturday, he had found the Palestinian leader "pessimistic." Arafat was also due to meet Netanyahu in the Swiss mountain resort on Sunday.

Mubarak said it was important to get progress towards opening an airport and a seaport in Gaza, under the control of Arafat's Palestinian Authority, and to implement other parts of overall accords on peace in the region.

Such moves were essential for the welfare of ordinary Palestinians. "Otherwise they will revolt against their regime," said Mubarak, speaking in English. Any people would rise up against a leader who was not seen to be doing all he could for them, he added.
